Pure-text answer needed; no tools required. Mutex explanation plus a small code sample.

A mutex (mutual exclusion lock) is a synchronization primitive that allows only one thread at a time to hold it, so code guarded by it runs as a critical section. Threads that try to acquire a mutex already held by another thread block until it is released, which prevents race conditions on shared data.

```python
import threading

lock = threading.Lock()
with lock:
    counter = 0  # critical section: only one thread at a time runs this block
```
